title: Dedicated SLA fast-path qualification for high-touch enterprise requests
creator: Sofia Ramos
description:
Summary: Create a concise, repeatable 'fast-path' qualification checklist and decision surface for incoming high-touch enterprise requests that ask for Dedicated capacity SLAs. Goal is to enable Sales/CS to triage requests in under 30 minutes, surface the right SLA profile (latency, reserved throughput, GPU family, burst policy) and escalate only when custom engineering work is required.

Background: We currently rely on a mix of long intake forms and ad-hoc Slack threads between Sales, Solutions, and Platform. This causes slow response times, inconsistent sizing recommendations, and unnecessary engineering involvement for common request patterns (e.g., stable RLHF training inference workloads vs. high-concurrency real-time chat). Building a fast-path will reduce cycle time to commitment and reduce false negatives in intake triage.

Primary objectives: 
1) Define a 12-question fast-path checklist that maps to an SLA profile (SLO latency bucket, reserved throughput QPS/TPS, GPU class recommendation, burst tolerance/burst credits, and fallback routing policy). 
2) Produce a one-page cheat sheet and a short form Sales script for initial call qualification. 
3) Implement a decision table that outputs one of: standard reserved profile (bronze/silver/gold), needs-custom-engineering, or redirect-to-hosted. 
4) Pilot the workflow with two AE teams and measure reduction in time-to-proposal and engineering touch rate.

Scope (in-scope): enterprise new-reservation requests for Dedicated pools where the ask is for SLA-backed latency/throughput guarantees. Excludes on-prem/Private air-gapped installs and non-binding exploratory demos.

Out of scope: building pricing models, final contract language, and capacity procurement automation. Those will be separate follow-ups after initial qualification is stable.
acceptance_criteria: A 12-question fast-path checklist is published in Confluence and a PDF quick-sheet exists for Sales
A decision table maps common workload fingerprints to predefined SLA profiles (bronze/silver/gold) and to 'needs-custom-engineering' when appropriate
Pilot with two AE teams completed: tracked 20 intakes with time-to-first-proposal metric reduced by >=40% relative to baseline
Engineering touch rate for qualifying intakes reduced by >=30% during pilot
Checklist and decision outputs include clear GPU-family recommendations and a default burst policy with documented trade-offs
Embedded links to evaluation artifacts: example sizing workbook, sample contract language snippets, and a recommended telemetry dashboard for SLO verification
decision_notes: Initial decision: favor conservative default GPU recommendations (A100y32 / H100-equivalent) for gold SLA and recommend quantized variants for silver if model supports it. For latency-sensitive >100ms SLOs consider dedicated low-latency thin-queue pools; for throughput-oriented RLHF inference prioritize GPU memory capacity and batch-friendly scheduling. We will not automatically recommend mixed-GPU pools in the fast-path — that remains a custom engineering workflow.
tradeoffs: Tighter fast-path reduces Slack/engineering handoffs but may underfit some edge workloads (e.g., very spiky RLHF with stringent token-level QoS). To mitigate we include an explicit 'uncertain' bucket that triggers a lightweight profiling run (1-2 days sample) before final commit. Conservative GPU recommendations will raise initial cost but reduce risk of regressions and SLA breaches.
outcomes_and_metrics: Time-to-first-proposal (target < 30 minutes for qualified fast-path), engineering touch rate, pilot conversion rate to reserved contracts, post-onboarding SLA incidents related to mismatched sizing. Telemetry: intake_form_completion_time, fastpath_accept_rate, engineering_escalation_count.
implementation_plan: 1) Draft checklist and decision table (PM + Solutions) — week 1. 2) Create Confluence doc + PDF quick-sheet + Sales script — week 1-2. 3) Build a simple Google Sheet sizing notebook that maps answers to profiles — week 2. 4) Train two AE pods and run 20 pilot intakes — week 3-6. 5) Collect metrics and iterate on thresholds — week 6-7. 6) Handoff to Ops for steady-state documentation and embed into CRM as a short form field — week 8.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Sales bypasses fast-path for perceived high-value deals. Mitigation: require AE to fill minimum fields in CRM and include checklist in initial intake; PM/Sales leadership alignment.
Risk: Checklist misclassifies complex workloads. Mitigation: explicit 'needs-custom-engineering' path and optional profiling run.
Risk: GPU recommendations lag model advances. Mitigation: set quarterly review and a lightweight model-to-hardware compatibility owner in Applied ML.
open_questions: What minimum telemetry must customers enable for SLA verification (logs vs traces)?
Should we offer an automated profiling job as a paid add-on or include it as part of onboarding?
What are explicit thresholds (latency/95th) for bronze/silver/gold buckets? (Proposed: bronze 95th <= 250ms, silver <= 150ms, gold <= 50ms)
